outcome: lack of MG treatment during perinatal period
cohort: The study included pregnancies in females aged 18-49 years identified from United States health insurance claims databases, with a subset diagnosed with myasthenia gravis (MG) and a larger age-adjusted total population for comparison.
finding: Myasthenia gravis (MG) was associated with a greater prevalence of adverse perinatal outcomes in both mothers and infants, including preeclampsia, preterm birth, and small for gestational age.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was more frequent among pregnancies in individuals with myasthenia gravis (42.9%) compared to the age-adjusted total population (36.7%).
